To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the neutron scattering method can be used in irrigated heavy cracking clay fields under arid tropical conditions to obtain reliable soil moisture information with a sampling density that can be afforded by the farmer.

the neutron scattering technique with a separate calibration for each depth and with temperature corrections is well suited for soil moisture determination on tenant irrigated fields in the Geziras clay soils under arid conditions; that the sampling density requirements for the 30 cms depth are 20 samples per 2.1 ha field if total experimental errors are to be kept within ±12.5% and that these sampling requirements increase to 24,28 and 33 if the total experimental error is to be kept within
in heavy cracking soils, with inhomogeneous watering, the sampling density required for reliable water use calculations is much larger than the 10–12 samples per field that is often recommended.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of minimum on-farm sampling densities for soil moisture monitoring in heavy clay soils in a semi-arid environment, with the Gezira scheme in Sudan as a case study.

the determination of minimum sampling density requirements and correction requirements to be able to use the neutron scattering technique for soil water monitoring in heavy cracking clay soils under arid conditions in the Gezria, central Sudan.
the practical application of neutron scattering for soil moisture measurements in the Gezirian environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the Geziras heavy cracking clay soils, sampling density requirements for neutron probe measurements of soil water in tenant irrigated end fields are very high, but that the required number of samples can be reduced by averaging several days of sampling.

the neutron scattering method can be used for water use efficiency studies under Gezira irrigation conditions with a reasonable sampling density and that the method is a powerful tool for studying the effects of inhomogeneous watering and soil management on the soil moisture distribution in heavy clay soils.

, in the Gezirian situation with its inhomogeneous irrigation, a sampling density of 24–33 samples at 30  cm is required to keep errors within 7.5–10% of the average soil moisture content at this depth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the case of the Gezirian soils and conditions, a minimum sampling density of 20 samples per hectare at 30  cm depth is needed if the errors are to remain below 12.5%, while at the more important lower depths only 10 samples per hectare are required for errors of 10% and below.
a sampling density of at least 20 neutron probe samples per ha is required to obtain a credible average soil moisture picture for a 2.5 ha end field.
the sampling density for soil moisture determination is a function of the depth of interest, the accuracy required and the inhomogeneities present in the field under consideration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the on-farm soil water distribution in irrigated heavy cracking clay soils is inhomogeneous, even in a relatively homogeneous field, and that sampling density requirements are high.
sampling density requirements for soil moisture measurement and water use efficiency calculations should be based on worst case analysis and not on a simple statistical analysis.
the neutron probe technique is well suited for the determination of average soil moisture content in the heavy cracking clays of the Geziza scheme, central Sudan.
